extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in AI ethics, NFTs, and video-game industry controversies
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic summary of a single incident in which a blockchain/NFT company (Voiceverse) used outputs from a non-commercial AI service (15.ai) without attribution and sold them as NFTs, provoking ethical, legal, and community backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of commercial use (15.ai terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: 15.ai's terms of service explicitly prohibited commercial use of the service and required proper attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using 15.ai-generated voices for NFTs violated the service's non-commercial terms; the page cites the terms as a substantive basis for labeling Voiceverse's actions as misuse/unauthorized commercial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to give proper attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Users of 15.ai must give proper credit when using the service for content creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voiceverse failed to attribute the voice samples to 15.ai in marketing materials and demos; lack of attribution was highlighted repeatedly by the developer and media as an ethical and contractual breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: No false representation of proprietary technology in marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must not market or demonstrably present others' outputs as their own proprietary technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voiceverse posted promotional videos claiming the voices were 'Powered By Voiceverse' while server logs showed the audio was generated by 15.ai and pitch-shifted to disguise the source—an example of deceptive marketing the article condemns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of plagiarism/theft
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriating another developer's work and selling it as one's own (or omitting credit) constitutes plagiarism/theft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News coverage and AI incident databases universally characterized Voiceverse's use of 15.ai output as 'stolen' or 'plagiarised'; the article uses server log evidence to show exact matches between 15.ai requests/responses and Voiceverse's promotional audio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for creator intent (non-commercial stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect the stated intent of tool creators who declare their projects non-commercial and request non-commercial use only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 15.ai's creator had explicitly stated no interest in NFTs or commercialisation; using the tool to support NFT sales violates that stated intent and is treated as an ethical transgression in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain permission and comply with licensing/IP requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using or monetizing voices or voice models, entities must secure permission/license and observe intellectual property constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The incident led to legal consequences and was later cited in litigation; the article notes allowed legal claims such as breach of contract, unfair business practices, and copyright infringement arising from unauthorized use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about data/model provenance and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about the source of synthesized voices and the provenance of models or audio used in demonstrations or products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights that Voiceverse intentionally pitch-shifted audio to hide provenance—an anti-pattern illustrating why provenance transparency is necessary to avoid deception and community backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deceptive attempts to obscure origins (e.g., pitch-shifting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate alteration of outputs to hide that they originated from another service is deceptive and unethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voiceverse's use of pitch-shifting to make 15.ai-generated voices 'unrecognizable' is presented as evidence of intentional misrepresentation and aggravating conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider environmental impact of NFTs/blockchain
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for and disclose environmental consequences of using blockchain/NFT technology due to energy consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics raised the environmental impact of NFTs as a core concern in the backlash; the article places this as one of several substantive grounds for public opposition to voice-NFT projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid predatory monetization practices in games
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from monetization models (including some NFTs) that replicate exploitative patterns (e.g., loot-box–style or predatory monetization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article situates NFTs as potentially predatory monetization in gaming and notes community sensitivity to perceived exploitation; this is offered as a normative standard industry actors violate at reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess labor impact: avoid devaluing human creators
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how generative AI products may displace or devalue paid work of professionals (e.g., voice actors) and address compensation/royalties appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage and actor responses raised concern that AI voices could jeopardize jobs and devalue voice acting; Voiceverse claimed actors would receive royalties, but community skepticism remained—pointing to labor/ethical criteria for responsible product design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be accountable: prompt remediation, apology, and corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: When misuse is revealed, companies and partners should acknowledge wrongdoing, apologize, remove offending content, and take corrective steps (including ending problematic partnerships if necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voiceverse issued an apology and deleted incriminating tweets; Troy Baker ended his partnership with Voiceverse—examples the article uses to show acceptable remediation, though public response judged the initial conduct severely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with community norms and expect reputational consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Product announcements involving contentious technologies (NFTs, AI voice cloning) should anticipate community norms and possible backlash; failing to do so risked severe reputational harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article documents universal negative reaction across gaming communities and press, demonstrating that ignoring community standards (or appearing dismissive) magnifies consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document incidents for research and policy (AI incident reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serious AI-related misuse should be recorded and classified by oversight/ethics databases to inform researchers, policymakers, and practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The incident was catalogued by AI Incident Database and AIAAIC (classified as theft/plagiarism), and cited by the MIT AI Risk Repository—presented as an important part of post-incident accountability and learning.
